coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Building 12 Plaza and Market Square
record.summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square (flanked by rehabilitated buildings and new construction, with an opening on 21st Street between Building 2 and Parcel D and a passageway through Buildings 2 and 12), the Building 12 entry plaza south of Building 12, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. Building 12 itself reopened in 2022 and Maryland Street's paving is done, but the plaza is a Phase 1 park still tied to adjacent vertical development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. Pier & Point chose these lots from its reading of the diagram and the satellite imagery; no document read ties these lots to the plaza. The lots do not cover all of the open ground the D4D draws around Buildings 2 and 12, so the earlier outline's extent is not reproduced. A building may sit back from the lot lines. The plaza is planned (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development).

notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.9), approximately 1.5 acres. Per Section 3.9, Market Square lies north of Building 12 (between Building 2 and Parcel D, entered from 21st St), the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, and the Maryland Street Platform along Building 12's Maryland St side; the mapped block spans Louisiana St to Maryland St.

changes.text: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 3 within approximately 25 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2042; 2042 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 25 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion.

open_questions: No completion date can be stated for the plaza. The Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) gives the Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) a park outside date of '1 year after Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (“TCO”) for Buildings 2 and 12' and Market Square (OS-2) '1 year after TCO for Building D' (Port Item 9B, Sept 22, 2017, Table A, p.8), and 9B says 'Parks must be completed between 12-18 months after completion of adjacent buildings' (p.7). Building 12's rehabilitation was completed in January 2022 (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026), but none of the sources cited here reports a TCO for Building 2 or Building D, and Item 11A says 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward' and that 'Developer has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels', so no calendar date follows. The DDA's Phase 3 outside date does not apply to this Phase 1 park, and the DDA's outside dates are extended while the down market delay lasts (extended to December 26, 2026); Item 11A also proposes to 'better align open spaces with revised vertical development schedule'.

No Port Commission schematic design approval or construction record for Market Square or the entry plaza was found; the interim events documented by the Port took place inside Building 12 and under Building 15, not on a finished plaza.

Whether the Building 15 structural frame is being retained (the D4D marks it 'pending structural feasibility study'): the Port's June 2025 deck shows Building 15 relocated over 22nd Street but does not say what will remain of it.

No openly licensed or public-record post-rehabilitation photo of Building 12 was found (checked Wikimedia Commons -- geosearch, category and title search all came up empty for anything dated 2022 or later). Perkins&Will's Building 12 wayfinding photography (by Bruce Damonte, via DNCO's case study) and Pier 70's own project photography are copyrighted, but their press/media contacts may grant editorial, non-commercial clearance on request -- worth revisiting if someone follows up with them.

Phase of Building 12 Plaza and Market Square: Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) lists Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) and Market Square (OS-2) among the Phase 1 parks, and Port Item 11A cites three acres of Phase 1 parks overall. Item 11A's 2026 phasing plan (Exhibit A) is an image whose text is not legible, so this record does not state the plaza's place in the proposed 2026 phasing.
